sections.content: The pluscuamperfecto looks back from one past moment to an earlier one. Use había or habían plus a participle when a later discovery explains something that had already happened.

items.spanish: Me di cuenta de que alguien había dejado una pista bajo la puerta.
items.english: I realised that someone had left a clue under the door.

items.spanish: Cuando volvimos, encontramos una maceta donde alguien había dejado una frase usada como pista.
items.english: When we returned, we found a flowerpot where someone had left a phrase used as a clue.

items.spanish: No entendí la carta porque mi padre había guardado la primera página y yo había olvidado leerla.
items.english: I did not understand the letter because my father had kept the first page and I had forgotten to read it.

items.spanish: Después de que habían cerrado el café, buscamos a quien nos había avisado que el tren saldría.
items.english: After the café had closed, we looked for the person who had told us the train would leave.

sections.content: Do not use the pluscuamperfecto for every past verb. It marks the event that is earlier than the past moment you are narrating: doy, dejó, supiste, reconocer, sorprenderme, llevaba, decirme, esperando y entenderlo are forms worth comparing.
